ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a 230 V, 50 Hz AC power source connected between the upper and lower two buses; the middle branch is a capacitor labeled C; the right branch is a load, labeled Z_L = 30∠40° Ω, and this load and the capacitor are connected in parallel across the same AC source. Reasoning: By the parallel admittance method, the load admittance is Y_L = 1/Z_L = (1/30)∠(-40°) S. Expanding gives Y_L = (1/30)(cos40° - j sin40°) = 0.0255 - j0.0214 S. The capacitor admittance is Y_C = jωC, where ω = 2πf = 2π(50) rad/s. When the source-end power factor is 1, the imaginary part of the total admittance is zero, so Im(Y_L + Y_C) = -0.0214 + ωC = 0. Therefore C = 0.0214 / (2π·50) = 6.81×10^-5 F = 68.1 μF.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what value of C will cause a unity power factor at the AC source?

method.method_draft: Use the image to identify the source frequency and the parallel topology. Convert the labeled load impedance Z_L = 30∠40° Ω into admittance Y_L = 1/Z_L. Because the capacitor is in parallel, add its admittance jωC to Y_L. Impose unity power factor by requiring the imaginary part of the total source admittance to be zero, solve C = -Im(Y_L)/ω at 50 Hz, and report the result in μF.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct admittance-cancellation route: it uses the parallel structure to make the source see a purely real total admittance, rather than computing branch currents or powers first.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the circuit diagram that a 230 V, 50 Hz AC source feeds two parallel branches: a capacitor labeled C and a load branch labeled Z_L = 30∠40° Ω. The capacitor is connected across the same two supply nodes as the load.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to know the requested unknown is the capacitance value that makes the AC source operate at unity power factor.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For unity power factor at the source, the net input admittance must have zero imaginary part. The load admittance is Y_L = 1/Z_L = (1/30)∠(-40°), whose susceptance is negative for an inductive load. The capacitor admittance is Y_C = jωC, with ω = 2π(50). Set Im(Y_L) + ωC = 0, so C = sin(40°)/(30·2π·50), then convert farads to microfarads to obtain about 68.1 μF.
